STACKIT (Schwarz Group).summary_note: STACKIT is the highest-scoring provider in the CloudSov framework by a significant margin. Its structural sovereignty advantages are exceptional: 100% privately held by a German family business with no external investors, no public listing, no US parent, explicit no-IPO policy, and contractual change-of-control clauses in government contracts (Dutch government framework, 2026). The €11 billion private investment in EU infrastructure — the largest in Schwarz Group history — and KRITIS critical infrastructure designation make it structurally the least acquisition-vulnerable and most resilient EU-controlled cloud provider assessed. Third-party validation is strong: BSI C5 Type 2 (August 2024), BSI strategic cooperation for German federal government classified workloads (March 2025), and EU Commission Cloud III selection at SEAL-3 level (April 2026, €180 million tender). The KMS product (HSM-backed, FIPS 140-2 Level 3, BYOK, available in both EU01 and EU02 regions) upgrades the customer key management position to Y. The principal weaknesses are structural and shared across the EU cloud market: (1) Intel/AMD processors and AMD SEV firmware are unavoidably non-EU (N on SOV-5 Q2, N on SOV-6 Q4); (2) The Aleph Alpha/Cohere merger (April 2026), with Schwarz investing €500M and STACKIT as designated hosting platform, introduces a non-EU corporate control dimension to the AI offering — all EU inference stays on STACKIT but the model governance is now majority Cohere/Canadian-controlled (P on SOV-3 Q5); (3) XM Cyber (Israeli Schwarz Digits subsidiary) and VERITAS (US backup partner) represent non-EU supply chain touchpoints (P on SOV-4 Q6, SOV-5 Q4); (4) Environmental disclosure at the STACKIT provider level lacks comprehensive quantified public reporting (P on SOV-8 Q3). Overall: approximately 33 Y, 6 P, 2 N across 41 questions.
